- Model tends to overestimate prices, especially in the early part of the forecast horizon (first 5–10 days).
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly — overcorrecting or lagging in mean reversion.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values, particularly when recent history shows downward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows strong mean reversion bias — model fails to adjust to recent low prices, holding onto high forecasts.
- Model underestimates volatility in the final 5–10 days of the forecast, especially when true values show sudden drops or corrections.
- When true values are clustered near a recent low, model continues to project higher values, indicating failure to recognize bottoming or reversal.
- Model reacts slowly to downward trends — often lags by 2–5 days in adjusting forecasts downward after a price drop.
- Model overfits to recent high values, especially when the last 5–10 days are high — fails to account for potential exhaustion or reversal.
